claimed_purpose.text: A local-first persistent conversational memory system that captures each conversation turn across multiple chat entry points and unifies them into local storage with hybrid retrieval.

mechanisms.text: Conversation messages are persisted to a separate `conversation_log` table; chunked summaries go to `conversation_chunks`; these are distinct from curated memories
Every conversation turn is stored verbatim via a Stop hook (Claude Code), Chrome sync extension (claude.ai), or channel adapters; no 'decide to save' step.
Experiences are persisted to a markdown file at a path derived from the IMPRINT_DATA_DIR environment variable, under a 'memory/bank/' directory structure.
Auto-surfacing: a UserPromptSubmit hook calls surfacing_search before the LLM sees the prompt and injects a <recall> block with ~6 related events.
Vector embeddings for memories: each memory can have a stored embedding blob (default model bge-m3), enabling semantic retrieval alongside FTS.
The bus is auto-pruned on every write: only the most recent MESSAGE_BUS_LIMIT (default 40) messages are retained; older rows are hard-deleted.
Multi-entry-point isolation resolved by design: different entry points all write into the same memory index.
Tasks are persisted to a database with status, prompt, session_id, and timestamps on submission
memory_pin marks a row so it bypasses importance/recency decay.
PRIVATE-tagged memories are filtered out of all search results

ledger.claim: Every conversation turn is stored verbatim to conversation_log automatically with no LLM decision step
ledger.quote: Every message stored verbatim — A Claude Code `Stop` hook + claude.ai sync + channel adapters call `log_message()` on every in/out turn. No "decide to save" step.
ledger.locator: README.md, table 'Automatic pipeline — the whole system'
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Curated memory_remember writes to a separate memories table distinct from the conversation_log, with a ranking boost
ledger.quote: Stores it in the curated `memories` table so future searches surface it with a small ranking boost
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Mixing embedding providers mid-lifecycle silently corrupts semantic search because cross-dimension cosine similarity returns 0
ledger.quote: Cross-boundary cosine sim always returns 0, search goes quietly blind — FTS still works, but the semantic channel goes dark for all data written before the switch
ledger.locator: README.md, section '⚠️ Embedding consistency — do not mix'
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Conversation log is distinct from curated memory: chunker LLM summaries may drop proper nouns, causing memory_search to miss hits that conversation_search (raw FTS5) would find
ledger.quote: `memory_search` only sees the chunk-layer index — the chunker's LLM summary may drop proper nouns (external system names, paper titles, library names). Then `memory_search` returns empty, but the raw `conversation_log` still has 20+ relevant messages.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Recall counter is updated on retrieval and influences future ranking
ledger.quote: Update recall count (frequently recalled memories maintain relevance)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: All data is stored locally in a SQLite database at ~/.imprint/memory.db; no cloud storage
ledger.quote: Your memory lives in a local database — not the cloud. ... `IMPRINT_DB` | `$IMPRINT_DATA_DIR/memory.db`
ledger.locator: README.md, opening description and configuration table
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Isolation is per-user local machine; no multi-user or per-session isolation described
ledger.quote: Everything you tell it stays — searchable across conversations, private, on your machine.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The message bus is a rolling log, not a curated memory store: it retains only the N most recent raw messages and hard-deletes older ones on every write.
ledger.quote: DELETE FROM message_bus WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM message_bus ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Content stored in the bus is lossy: messages longer than 200 characters are truncated before persistence.
ledger.quote: content: message content (auto-truncated to 200 chars)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The bus is read into context via bus_format, which renders it as a human-readable block labeled '# Recent Messages' with timestamps and direction arrows.
ledger.quote: lines = ["# Recent Messages\n"]
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Messages are written to conversation_log by log_message(); dedup is handled by external_id collision so the same transcript entry is never stored twice
ledger.quote: external_id (the transcript entry uuid) lets log_message drop anything that slips through twice
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Capture is triggered by a Claude Code Stop hook; stdin carries transcript_path and session_id
ledger.quote: A `Stop` hook hands this script the current transcript path; we incrementally read the new lines
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Stored message content is truncated to 8000 chars with an ellipsis appended; no summarization or extraction is performed
ledger.quote:
if len(text) > MAX_CHARS:
                text = text[:MAX_CHARS] + "..."
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Capture errors are silently swallowed so a capture failure cannot interrupt the Claude Code turn
ledger.quote: Stays silent and never raises so a capture hiccup can't break the turn.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory write path: raw messages in conversation_log are chunked, summarized by LLM into a recap + extracted memories (facts), and stored in conversation_chunks and chunk_facts — curated memory is separate from the raw log
ledger.quote: INSERT OR IGNORE INTO conversation_chunks (start_msg_id, end_msg_id, msg_count, platforms, summary, keywords, embedding, start_time, end_time) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieve policy: all chunks with non-null embeddings are always scored; there is no adaptive or conditional skip — every chunk participates in every search
ledger.quote:
rows = db.execute(
            """SELECT id, start_msg_id, end_msg_id, msg_count, platforms,
                      summary, keywords, embedding, start_time, end_time
               FROM conversation_chunks
               WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL"""
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Isolation is per session_id within a batch: messages from different sessions are grouped separately before chunking, so memory chunks are never cross-session
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Forget / deletion: chunk_facts uses ON DELETE CASCADE from conversation_chunks, so deleting a chunk row removes its extracted facts; no other explicit forget or hide-at-retrieve path is present in this file
ledger.quote: chunk_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES conversation_chunks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Thinking blocks from assistant messages are stripped before summarization, so internal chain-of-thought is not persisted into memory
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Causal edge blacklist filters generic emotional/relationship topic words from keyword-overlap gating, to avoid spurious causal links between unrelated emotional conversations
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Routine/heartbeat chunks (reminders to drink water, daily briefings, memory maintenance tasks) are filtered out before causal edge building
ledger.quote:
routine_kw = ['喝水', '早安简报', '记忆整理', '记忆衰减', '去重',
                      'send_telegram', '补剂', '水杯', '提醒喝']
        def is_routine(r):
            s = (r.get('summary','') + r.get('keywords','')).lower()
            return any(kw in s for kw in routine_kw) or r.get('platforms') == 'heartbeat'
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Summarizer provider chain: OpenAI-compatible endpoint (when SUMMARY_API_KEY set) → Cloudflare Workers AI → Gemini → Ollama local fallback
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: conversation_log is a raw message log (every turn stored), not a curated memory extract. conversation_vectors is a companion index of per-message embeddings over that log.
ledger.quote:
SELECT c.id, c.platform, c.direction, c.speaker, c.content,
                      c.session_id, c.entrypoint, c.created_at, v.embedding
               FROM conversation_vectors v
               JOIN conversation_log c ON c.id = v.msg_id
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieve policy is always-retrieve over the full vector table with no score threshold beyond sim > 0; limit is capped at 50.
ledger.quote:
limit = max(1, min(int(limit or 10), 50))
...if sim <= 0:
                continue
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Edge strength update on retrieval acts as a reinforcement/decay mechanism: frequently surfaced topic links grow stronger; dormant links are reactivated on access.
ledger.quote:
strength = min(strength + 0.1, 5.0),
                       last_surfaced_at = datetime('now'),
                       status = CASE WHEN status='dormant' THEN 'active' ELSE status END
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memories and conversation log are distinct stores: `memories` holds curated facts with importance and category; `conversation_log` is the raw turn-by-turn archive.
ledger.quote:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS memories (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            content TEXT NOT NULL,
            category TEXT DEFAULT 'general',
            source TEXT DEFAULT 'cc',
            tags TEXT DEFAULT '[]',
            importance INTEGER DEFAULT 5,
            recalled_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0, ...
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory deletion cascades to the vector embedding and tag tables via ON DELETE CASCADE, meaning deleting a memory also removes its embedding and tags.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: FTS index strips <think> blocks from conversation_log content at index time to prevent hidden reasoning from polluting keyword search results, while preserving full content in the archive column.
ledger.quote: We keep the full content (incl. think) in conversation_log for archival, and strip it only at the index/display layer.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory edges track `surfaced_count` and `used_count` separately, distinguishing when an association was shown to the user from when it was actually acted upon.
ledger.quote:
surfaced_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            used_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: A separate `bank_chunks` table with file path and mtime supports a lore/backstory bank of chunked documents distinct from in-conversation memory writes.
ledger.quote: BANK_DIR = DATA_DIR / "memory" / "bank"
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Test messages are isolated from memory surfacing and search by an `is_test` flag on conversation_log, not by a separate table or session boundary.
ledger.quote: is_test=1 so the chunker, surfacing, and search pools all skip them.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Curated memories are persisted to SQLite with content, category, source, tags, importance, timestamp, and a separate embedding blob table
ledger.quote:
cursor = db.execute(
        """INSERT INTO memories (content, category, source, tags, importance, created_at)
           VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
        (content, category, source, tags_json, importance, ts),
    )
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Three distinct stores: memories (curated facts), conversation_log (raw message log), conversation_chunks (chunk summaries); these are separate pools, not one unified log
ledger.quote:
pools:    subset of ["memory", "bank", "chunk", "conversation"]; None = ["memory", "bank", "chunk"]
          - memory: curated facts extracted by the extractor
          - bank:   markdown notes under memory/bank/
          - chunk:  conversation chunks (index layer; hits expand to raw messages)
          - conversation: raw conversation_log rows (opt-in; used by conversation_search)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Conflict/supersession on write: semantic similarity 0.85–0.92 marks old memory as historical (superseded_by set), not deleted; ≥0.92 skips the new write entirely
ledger.quote:
- Semantic similarity ≥ 0.92 → skip (nearly identical)
    - Semantic similarity 0.85~0.92 → supersede: old memory marked historical, new one stored
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Forget is a hard delete from both memories and memory_vectors tables, triggered by keyword substring match
ledger.quote:
db.execute("DELETE FROM memory_vectors WHERE memory_id = ?", (row["id"],))
        db.execute("DELETE FROM memories WHERE id = ?", (row["id"],))
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Decay is a soft-delete path: memories reaching importance=0 get superseded_by=-1 (archived), not hard-deleted
ledger.quote: UPDATE memories SET importance = 0, superseded_by = -1, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Recency time decay is disabled in search scoring; old memories rank by relevance not age
ledger.quote: WEIGHT_RECENCY = 0.0  # time decay disabled — old hits rank by relevance, not age
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieve uses RRF fusion across FTS5 and vector channels; minimum score threshold of 0.40 applied before ranking
ledger.quote:
MIN_SCORE = 0.40
    ranked = [r for r in results.values() if r["final_score"] >= MIN_SCORE]
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Surfacing auto-recall skips content already in the current Claude Code session context by reading the session JSONL to find the earliest visible timestamp
ledger.quote:
surfacing skips anything already visible in cc's prompt
    context — both content authored in the live session AND content that
    a forge-reload carried over from a previous session. Detection: read
    the session's JSONL, take the earliest message timestamp as the
    context cutoff
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: PRIVATE-tagged memories are filtered from all search results
ledger.quote:
# Filter out PRIVATE-tagged memories
    results = [r for r in results if not (r.get("content", "").startswith("[PRIVATE]"))]
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Pinned memories bypass time-decay in search reranking
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Session-level surfacing dedup: surfaced IDs are written to a per-session file so the same item is not re-surfaced in the same session
ledger.quote:
_surfaced_file = (_surfaced_dir / f"{current_session}.ids") if current_session else None
    _seen_surfaced: set[str] = set()
    if _surfaced_file and _surfaced_file.exists():
        _seen_surfaced = set(_surfaced_file.read_text().split())
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Daily log is append-only and stored separately from curated memories; it is not searchable via the same hybrid search path
ledger.quote:
def daily_log(text: str) -> str:
    """Append to today's daily log."""
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Embedding provider must not be switched mid-store; mixing dimensions corrupts cosine similarity; no auto-fallback to a different provider
ledger.quote:
No cross-provider fallback. Switching providers mid-store mixes vector
    dimensions and silently breaks cosine search, so a failure surfaces a
    throttled warning and returns None (callers degrade to FTS5/LIKE) rather
    than quietly embedding with a different backend.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: MEMORY.md is a lightweight index rebuilt after each write; it contains date + keyword per line and is not the primary search surface
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Curated memory store separates facts, events, and insights from a raw conversation log and a daily log
ledger.quote: category: facts (persistent truths/preferences/commitments) / events (things that happened, with dates) / insights (reflections/observations/lessons)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Decay moves memories to an archived (hidden from search) state at importance 0 rather than deleting them
ledger.quote: Reaches 0 → archived (hidden from search).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Pinned memories are exempt from time-decay in search, providing a stable high-priority recall layer
ledger.quote: Pinned memories bypass time-decay in search. Keep under 20.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieval is hybrid: FTS5 keyword, vector semantic, and exact-match channels fused with RRF across memory, bank, and chunk pools
ledger.quote:
Combines FTS5 keyword, vector semantic, and exact-match channels with per-pool reranking.
    Falls back to keyword-only if no embedding provider is configured.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: recalled_count is tracked per memory and used in stale detection, implying retrieval events are logged
ledger.quote: imp={m_item['importance']} recalled={m_item['recalled_count']}
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Graph edges track surfaced_count and used_count per edge, distinguishing retrieval from actual use
ledger.quote: (surfaced:{e['surfaced_count']}, used:{e['used_count']})
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Task records including prompt, status, session_id, and timestamps are persisted in a database table cc_tasks
ledger.quote: INSERT INTO cc_tasks (prompt, status, source, session_id, created_at) VALUES (?, 'pending', ?, ?, ?)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Session resumption is implemented by passing a stored session_id to the --resume flag of the claude subprocess
ledger.quote:
Pass session_id to resume a previous session.
...
if session_id:
            cmd.extend(["--resume", session_id])
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The session_id is updated in the store after each task run, propagating the new session state for subsequent turns
ledger.quote:
new_session_id = parsed.get("session_id", "")
...
db.execute(
        "UPDATE cc_tasks SET status = ?, result = ?, session_id = ?, completed_at = ? WHERE id = ?",
        (status, output_text, new_session_id or session_id, now_str(), task_id),
    )
ledger.locator: _execute_task function, JSON parse block and final db.execute
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Task store contains the full prompt text and result output, making it a message/task log rather than a curated memory store
ledger.quote: SELECT id, prompt, status, result, session_id, created_at, started_at, completed_at FROM cc_tasks WHERE id = ?
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Every turn is stored verbatim automatically via log_message(); no LLM decision required to persist.
ledger.quote: A Claude Code Stop hook + claude.ai sync + channel adapters call log_message() on every in/out turn. No "decide to save" step.
ledger.locator: README.md, table "Automatic pipeline — the whole system", row "Every message stored verbatim"
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Conversations are segmented into events with LLM-generated summaries (chunk log, not raw transcript) as the primary retrieval unit above conversation_log.
ledger.quote: incremental_chunk_update runs on a schedule, groups consecutive messages into chunks, generates a one-paragraph LLM summary + keywords per chunk
ledger.locator: README.md, table "Automatic pipeline — the whole system", row "Segment conversations into 'events'"
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieve path injects ~6 related events as a <recall> block into the prompt before the LLM sees it, on every user prompt.
ledger.quote: A UserPromptSubmit hook calls surfacing_search before the LLM sees the prompt and injects a <recall> block with ~6 related events
ledger.locator: README.md, table "Automatic pipeline — the whole system", row "Auto-surface relevant context on every prompt"
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Forget is supported at three levels: memory_delete (single row by ID), memory_forget (bulk delete by keyword), memory_decay (gradual importance fade).
ledger.quote: memory_forget: Delete all memories containing a keyword. … memory_decay: Gradually fade memories that haven't been recalled. Preview first, then apply.
ledger.locator: README.md, MCP Tools table "Memory CRUD" and "Memory Maintenance"
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Pinning prevents decay; unpinning restores normal aging — explicit decay bypass mechanism.
ledger.quote: Marks the row pinned — bypasses any importance/recency decay
ledger.locator: README.md, section "Optional curation tools", table row memory_pin
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Semantic search silently degrades (returns 0 cosine similarity) if embedding provider is switched mid-database; FTS still functions but semantic channel is dead for pre-switch data.
ledger.quote: search silently goes half-blind — FTS still works, but the semantic channel is dead for everything written before the switch
ledger.locator: README.md, section "⚠️ Embedding consistency — DO NOT MIX"
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Chunker LLM summaries can drop proper nouns, causing memory_search to return nothing for named entities even when conversation_log contains 20+ matching raw messages — a known retrieval continuity gap.
ledger.quote: the chunker's LLM summaries can drop proper nouns (e.g. system names, paper titles, library names). When that happens, memory_search returns nothing even though the raw conversation_log still has 20+ matching messages.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memories are typed into categories: facts (preferences, truths), events (things that happened), insights (reflections).
ledger.quote: Store a memory. Categories: facts (preferences, truths), events (things that happened), insights (reflections). Auto-deduplicates.
ledger.locator: README.md, MCP Tools table "Memory CRUD", row memory_remember
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Graph edges between memories carry typed relations (causal, analogy, evolution, contradiction); linked memories surface together in search.
ledger.quote: Link two memories with a relationship (causal, analogy, evolution, contradiction, etc). Linked memories show up together in search.
ledger.locator: README.md, MCP Tools table "Graph Structure", row memory_add_edge
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Store is per-user-machine (local SQLite at ~/.imprint/memory.db); no per-session or per-agent isolation described.
ledger.quote: Your memory lives in a local database — not the cloud. … Data lives in ~/.imprint/
ledger.locator: README.md, top description and Quick Start

ledger.claim: The experience_append tool writes to a file at memory/bank/experience.md, with the base directory controlled by the IMPRINT_DATA_DIR environment variable, defaulting to the current directory.
ledger.quote: exp_path = Path(os.environ.get("IMPRINT_DATA_DIR", ".")) / "memory" / "bank" / "experience.md"
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: imprint-memory is a local-first persistent conversational memory system capturing every turn across multiple entry points into a unified local database with hybrid FTS5+vector retrieval.
ledger.quote: imprint-memory 是一个本地优先的持久对话记忆系统。它通过 Claude Code Hook、claude.ai 扩展和 Telegram 适配器捕获每轮对话，再用 FTS5 与语义向量进行混合检索。
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: All entry-point adapters write into a single shared memory index, so switching platforms does not break continuity.
ledger.quote: 多个聊天入口写进同一份记忆索引
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Platform is Python, self-hosted, supporting stdio and HTTP MCP interfaces.
